_doc: Slide 20, the report card: exchanges and lending protocols graded by the rule below, one row per component, plus the five incidents of incidents.json graded F. Every row's 'fact' is a measurement or a documented choice, stated as measured and never as a defect; a library's or protocol's documented precision is not a defect; no loss is claimed at any exchange. 'fact' is what the slide may print beside the name (<= 48 chars); 'measured' says how the number was obtained; 'source.ref' is the repo JSON that holds the number or the protocol's source file at a pinned commit; 'claim' is the T-id in talk/briefs/tiers-provenance.md, which quotes the line or shows the computation. Incident rows copy name, date, loss, lossUsd, rounding (as 'measured') and source (as 'note') verbatim from incidents.json. Generated 2026-10-30; rows the draft listed but that could not be pinned are listed in the provenance note under 'not pinned'. 2026-10-30: the user's rule moves under-10-digit rows and in-domain reverts to F (Aave v3, Morpho Blue, SparkLend, FraxLend, Euler v2). 'short' is the chip's name on the slide where 'name' is too long to fit; 'name' stays the row's full name for the notes.

rule.S: S · correctly rounded or integer-exact: every answer the closest the format holds (for an exchange: the swap maths is exact integer arithmetic, nothing to round)
rule.A: A · about 30 correct digits on the talk's data
rule.B: B · the format's 18 decimals, as documented; zero below 10^-18 is the floor; a small documented precision choice
rule.C: C · 10 correct digits or more, but fewer than the format holds; a model measurably off its documented value
rule.F: F · under 10 correct digits, a revert inside the domain, or a rounding step that lost money (the user's rule, 2026-10-30)

rows.name: Uniswap v2 swap
rows.fact: x·y = k checked in whole units · fee 3 of 1000
rows.measured: UniswapV2Pair.swap requires balance0Adjusted·balance1Adjusted >= reserve0·reserve1·1000² with balanceAdjusted = balance·1000 − amountIn·3, all in uint256; the only rounding is the integer output the caller asks for.

rows.name: Uniswap v3/v4 swap step
rows.fact: 512-bit mulDiv · every step rounds to the pool
rows.measured: SqrtPriceMath and SwapMath compute the next sqrt price and the amounts with FullMath.mulDiv (exact 512-bit intermediate) and a stated rounding direction per quantity ('Always rounds up, because in the exact output case ... we need to move the price at least far enough'); nothing is approximated. v4-core carries the same libraries.

rows.name: Curve StableSwap (3pool, ng)
rows.fact: D and y by integer Newton, stopped within 1 unit
rows.measured: get_D and get_y iterate in uint256 and stop when |D − Dprev| <= 1 and |y − y_prev| <= 1 ('Equality with the precision of 1'): the invariant and the swap output are integers to the last unit, in both the 2020 3pool and stableswap-ng.

rows.name: Aerodrome stable pool
rows.fact: x³y + y³x solved in whole units · nearest y
rows.measured: Pool._get_y iterates in integer 1e18-normalised units and returns y or y + 1 ('There's no closer answer than y + 1'); the swap check _k(balance) < _k(reserve) is integer.

source.licence: Pool.sol header: GPL-3.0-or-later (repo licence field unset; the draft said BUSL)

rows.name: Trader Joe LB swap in a bin
rows.fact: 128.128 multiply-shift · rounded toward the pool
rows.measured: BinHelper.getAmounts: the bin's max amount in is reserve·2^128/price rounded up (shiftDivRoundUp / mulShiftRoundUp) and the amount out is amountIn·price >> 128 rounded down; integer arithmetic on a 128.128 price, no approximation.

rows.name: Uniswap v3/v4 TickMath
rows.fact: sqrt price · 29 digits at tick ±1 · 9 at the end
rows.measured: getSqrtRatioAtTick transcribed (constants parsed from the file; each within 0.49 units of 2^128·1.0001^(−2^(i−1))) and compared with mpmath sqrt(1.0001^tick)·2^96 at 120 digits: 28–29 correct digits for |tick| <= 23027, 31–33 at 100000–200000, 18–27 at ±500000, 19 at +887272 and 9 at −887272, where the Q64.96 fixed point holds about 32 significant bits. The result is rounded up, not to nearest.

rows.name: Trader Joe LB bin price
rows.fact: price from bin id · 26 to 39 correct digits
rows.measured: PriceHelper.getPriceFromId = getBase(binStep).pow(id − 2^23) in 128.128, transcribed: the base (1 + binStep/10000)·2^128 is floored (relative −4e-40); against exact (1 + s/10000)^e·2^128 at 120 digits the price has 39 digits at e = ±1, 33–36 at the mid range, 34 at binStep 1 or 10 with e = ±10000 and 26 at binStep 100 with e = ±3000, where the truncation of each squaring accumulates.

rows.name: Uniswap v3 TWAP (OracleLibrary)
rows.fact: mean tick floored before pricing · under 1 bp
rows.measured: OracleLibrary.consult sets arithmeticMeanTick = int24(tickCumulativesDelta / secondsAgo) and 'Always round[s] to negative infinity'; one tick is a factor 1.0001, so the floor moves the price it reports by less than 1 bp. The live +0.787 bp figure of the draft (USDC/WETH, block 26258017) was not re-run and is not claimed.

rows.name: Pendle market exchange rate
rows.fact: E = e^rt in 18-decimal LogExpMath, as documented
rows.measured: MarketMathCore._getExchangeRateFromImpliedRate: 'The formula is E = e^rt'; exchangeRate = LogExpMath.exp(rt) and the implied rate is exchangeRate.ln(), both Balancer's 18-decimal LogExpMath. Not integer-exact, so B rather than the draft's S.

rows.name: GMX v2 price impact
rows.fact: impact exponent by 18-decimal pow, as documented
rows.measured: Precision.applyExponentFactor converts the 30-decimal float to 18 decimals, calls PRBMathUD60x18.pow and converts back ('we need to convert float (30 decimals) to 60x18 (18 decimals) and then back to 30 decimals'); below 1.0 it returns 0 ('pow doesn't work for x less than one'). Not integer-exact, so B rather than the draft's S.

rows.name: Curve twocrypto-ng get_y
rows.fact: Newton on y stops at 1e-14 of y, its own limit
rows.measured: TwocryptoMath.get_y sets convergence_limit = max(x_j // 10**14, D // 10**14, 100) and returns when the step is below max(convergence_limit, y // 10**14): a stated stopping precision of 1e-14 relative in 18-decimal arithmetic. The draft's 7.4e-16 measurement was not re-run and is not claimed.

rows.name: Algebra V1 dynamic fee
rows.fact: sigmoid fee by an 8-term e^x series · cut at 6γ
rows.measured: AdaptiveFee.exp sums e^(x/g)·g^8 through the x^8 term ('e^(x/g) = 1 + x/g + x^2/(2*g^2) + ...') and sigmoid returns alpha or 0 once x >= 6·g; the fee itself is a uint16. A fee policy, graded as documented.

rows.name: Compound v3 (Comet)
rows.fact: 15-decimal index · simple interest between calls
rows.measured: BASE_INDEX_SCALE = 1e15 and accruedInterestIndices adds mulFactor(index, rate·timeElapsed) to the stored uint64 index: linear between accruals, floored to the 1e15 grid. A documented precision choice, so B rather than the draft's C.

rows.name: Maverick v2 TickMath
rows.fact: sqrt price · 17 digits at tick ±1 · 11 at MAX
rows.measured: tickSqrtPrice transcribed with the 19 constants parsed from the file: the constants' relative error doubles from 5.5e-18 (i = 0) to 1.4e-12 (i = 18), so each holds 17.3 down to 11.8 digits; the D18 result against exact sqrt(1.0001^tick)·1e18 has 17 correct digits at tick ±1, 14 at ±1000, 13 at ±10000, 12 at ±100000 and 11 at ±322378 (MAX_TICK), in a format that holds 18. Every user of a pool sees the same grid; no loss is claimed. The draft's 'constants as float64 1.0001' does not hold: float64 1/sqrt(1.0001) in Q128 is 0xfffcb933bd6fb8000..., not the file's 0xfffcb933bd6fad9d....

rows.name: Aave v3 (Ethereum)
rows.fact: 74 live positions · median 8.6 interest digits
rows.measured: docs/benchmarks/accrual-deployed.json: 74 live Aave v3 positions at block 26206698 (39 borrow, 35 supply) against a 200-digit truth of the formula Aave states (e^(rt) for debt; per-second compounding of the liquidity rate, the APY Aave displays, for supply): correct digits of interest min 0.0, median 8.6, of balance median 13.5. Deployed code pinned to aave-v3-origin v3.7.0 and verified against the mainnet bytecode in the same file.

rows.name: Morpho Blue
rows.fact: 252 live markets · median 7.1 digits of interest
rows.measured: docs/benchmarks/accrual-deployed.json: 252 live Morpho Blue markets at block 26206698 against e^(integral of the rate) on the IRM's stated path: correct digits of interest median 7.1 over all 252 (7.41 over the 210 idle under 7 days; 1.7 over the 42 idle 7 days or more, most at 100% utilisation). wTaylorCompounded: 'the sum of the first three non-zero terms of a Taylor expansion of e^(nx) - 1'.

rows.name: SparkLend
rows.fact: cubic term 0 below 3.1536% APR · 8.8 digits a day
rows.measured: sparklend-v1-core MathUtils (the Aave v3.0.2 form): basePowerThree = (rate.rayMul(rate) / SECONDS_PER_YEAR²).rayMul(rate) / SECONDS_PER_YEAR floors to 0 for every rate up to 31535999842319999605799990 RAY = 3.1536% APR (binary search over the integer formula; 1 at the next RAY unit). At 3% APR the dropped term is 1.1e-9 of one idle day's interest, 1.0e-6 of 30 days', 1.5e-4 of a year's. Repo code; the deployed pool was not re-verified against bytecode. Graded by the user's rule (under 10 digits is F): Aave v3.0.2's integer binomial in ray, one day at 3% APR, against continuous compounding e^(rt) - 1 (the model the binomial approximates), mpmath at 60 digits: 8.8 correct digits of the day's interest.

rows.name: FraxLend VariableInterestRate V2
rows.fact: 5 idle days at 100% · ×3.5, half-life says ×5.66
rows.measured: docs/benchmarks/ladder.json, scenario adaptive-rate, input 'reference' (4% APR, 100% utilisation, a day per step, FraxLend's deployed half-life of two days), N = 5: FraxLend 4.439370876e-9 per second from rate0 1.26839167935e-9 (×3.5000), where 2^(5/2) gives the truth 7.17510686e-9 (×5.6569); 1.2 correct digits (over the scenario: min 0.2, median 1.4, max 4.7 at N = 1). The code multiplies by (1 + δ²Δt/H), which equals the documented 2^(Δt/H) only at Δt = H.

rows.name: Euler v2 IRMAdaptiveCurve
rows.fact: rate at target, one idle day · −0.28% / +0.42%
rows.measured: docs/benchmarks/ladder.json, scenario adaptive-rate, at Euler's deployed ADJUSTMENT_SPEED (100 per year), one idle day then one update: input 'euler-speed' (100% utilisation) relative error −0.00279481; input 'euler-halving' (0% utilisation) +0.00421513, against r0·e^(speed·err·t), the formula the contract's comment states. ExpLib.wExp reduces x by ln 2 and computes 'e^r with a 2nd-order Taylor polynomial'.

rows.name: Resupply
rows.measured: The exchange rate, 1e36 divided by that price, came out just under one half. Integer division floored it to zero.

rows.name: Bunni v2
rows.measured: Forty-four withdrawals, each rounding the idle balance the way the team believed safe. Active USDC 28 base units to 4; liquidity down 84%.
